Read with these limitations
Realized returns use supplied unadjusted prices, explicit FX and booked net dividends/fees. Unrecorded costs or events are absent.
UTC calendar-day closes and 365 observations/year; no market-calendar alignment or automatic price carry-forward.
XIRR includes the closing marked value; it is not a cash-only realized-profit figure.
Supplied data quality is not independently verified. This report makes no GIPS compliance claim.
Short track record: annualized time-weighted return is withheld; ratios and tails are descriptive and statistically uncertain.
Selected-period report: opening market value is treated as invested capital for XIRR, not an original deposit.

Flow segments and opening exposures
Contribution conventions and limitations
Contributions explain recorded TWR in percentage points, not security returns or risk contributions.
Local capital P&L, net dividends and fees use segment-end FX. Opening equity/cash receive FX changes; conversion principal is separate. Price/FX interaction is assigned to price.
This endpoint allocation is not transaction-time FX attribution. Supplied quotes and booked events are not independently certified.
Cash has no modeled interest; only booked events and marked FX can contribute. Standalone fees and conversion effects remain separate from equity rankings.
Closed equities remain included. Security UUIDs identify holdings; historical sector classifications are unavailable, so no sector aggregation is inferred.
Forward wealth linking allocates compounding to later increments; alternative linking conventions can assign different component results while reconciling to the same TWR.

The return difference is portfolio TWR minus benchmark return in percentage points. Relative wealth divides their compounded growth. Daily differences do not compound into the return difference.

These are descriptive sample estimates. Annualization is a mathematical scaling convention, not a forecast of one-year returns. This short sample can produce extreme and unstable ratios, beta and annualized values; it does not establish persistent skill.

Review benchmark identity and evidence
Comparison conventions and limitations
Historical benchmark comparison is descriptive evidence, not an expected return or decision.
Portfolio returns include booked net dividends and fees; benchmark gross/net and hedging conventions can differ. A net index does not necessarily include investor management costs.
UTC calendar-day intervals and 365 observations/year. Supplied weekend levels and quote-age settings are explicit evidence, not automatic carry-forward or trading-calendar alignment.
Tracking error is realized sample dispersion of arithmetic active returns, not ex-ante tracking risk or position risk contribution. Square-root annualization assumes stable variance and no serial correlation; stale/repeated levels can distort it.
Information ratio uses annualized arithmetic mean active return, not a CAGR difference. Beta/correlation are centered paired sample moments; no alpha or factor inference is claimed.
Benchmark identity, total-return basis, marks and suitability are supplied, not certified. Selection is explicit for this account/report; saved identity settings supply no provider levels.
Short sample: estimates are unstable and not evidence of persistent skill.
